brief.goal: Promote grand opening of Sunrise Coffee

audience.description: Residents within a 2-mile radius of the shop in downtown Austin

brief.desiredRecipientAction: Scan a QR code to redeem a free coffee coupon

primarySuccessMetric.description: Number of QR code scans redeeming the free coffee coupon

brief.offer: Free coffee coupon via QR code scan
brief.otherRequirements: No logo needed on the postcard

transcript.content: I own a coffee shop and want to send 500 postcards to residents near my shop to promote our grand opening. I want people to scan a QR code for a free coffee coupon. My shop is called Sunrise Coffee, website sunrisecoffee.com. Keep it warm and inviting, no logo needed.

Love this concept — a grand opening postcard with a free coffee QR coupon is a great way to drive foot traffic right out of the gate. Quick question: where should that QR code actually send people — a specific coupon landing page on your site, or something like a Google/Apple Wallet pass or a simple "show this at checkout" image? And do you have your shop's address and phone number you'd like printed on the postcard so people can find you easily?
sunrisecoffee.com/coupon is the landing page. Address is 45 Sunrise Ave, Austin, TX. Phone is 512-555-0199.

Perfect, that gives me everything I need for a strong first draft: a warm, inviting postcard for Sunrise Coffee's grand opening, sent to 500 nearby residents, featuring a QR code linking to sunrisecoffee.com/coupon for a free coffee redemption, plus your address and phone number, and no logo. Let's move on to reviewing the full brief together.
